v: They said therefore to him, “Who are you?” Jesus said to them, “Just what I have been saying to you from the beginning.
I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you. However he who sent me is true; and the things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.”
They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.
Jesus therefore said to them, “When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and I do nothing of myself, but as my Father taught me, I say these things.
He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, for I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”
As he spoke these things, many believed in him.
b: The core question of this passage is:
This is not only the Pharisees' question but the most important question in every person's life. For how you know Jesus will determine how you live, and also your eternal destination.
“They said therefore to him, ‘Who are you?’”
It was not the first time they had heard Jesus, nor the first time they had seen Him. They had already heard His teaching and seen His miracles, yet they still did not know Him.
The problem was not insufficient information but a heart that was not open.
Today also many people know things about Jesus without truly knowing Him. They know His name but do not know who He is.
“Just what I have been saying to you from the beginning.”
“I have been telling you who I am all along; you just were not willing to accept it.”
From the beginning He kept revealing:
He is the bread of life; the light of the world; the one who came from the Father; the giver of eternal life; the Christ.
But if people are unwilling to believe, even the clearest truth cannot get in.
“The things which I heard from him, these I say to the world.”
Jesus was not speaking His own words; He was bringing the Father's heart to the world. He did not represent Himself; He represented the Father.
This is also His greatest difference from the people of the world:
The world speaks from itself; Jesus speaks from the Father.
The world seeks its own glory; Jesus seeks the Father's glory.
The world lives by its own will; Jesus lives in the Father's will.
“They didn’t understand that he spoke to them about the Father.”
This again shows that without the Holy Spirit's enlightenment, people cannot truly understand spiritual things.
Jesus kept speaking of the Father, but they stayed at an earthly level of understanding. They heard words but did not hear life.
Then Jesus spoke a startling prophecy:
“When you have lifted up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he.”
“Lifted up the Son of Man” refers to the cross.
After I am crucified, raised, and glorified, you will finally know who I am.
The cross is not a defeat but the deepest revelation. Jesus' true glory is not an earthly throne but self-giving on the cross.
This is the deepest core of Jesus' life: self-denial.
He never relied on Himself; did not follow His own will; did not seek His own glory; did not do what the Father had not asked Him to do.
He lived completely in the Father.
Then verse 29 is a most precious sentence:
“He who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone.”
Why was the Father always with Him?
“I always do the things that are pleasing to him.”
Jesus' greatest peace was not smooth circumstances; not people's support; not the absence of enemies; but knowing that the Father was with Him.
And the key to the Father's presence is obedience.
True presence is not only a feeling but a life aligned with God.
“As he spoke these things, many believed in him.”
When the truth is spoken clearly, there are always some willing to believe.
Not everyone rejects; there are always humble hearts who see Jesus in the true light.
First, the most important question in life is: “Who do you say Jesus is?”
Second, Jesus never spoke or acted on His own. He lived completely in the Father.
Third, spiritual blindness is not that people did not hear but that they were unwilling to accept. Without surrender, people cannot truly know Jesus.
Fourth, the cross is Jesus' true glory. His victory is not exalting Himself but giving Himself to the very end.
Fifth, the Father's presence is deeply related to obedience. Jesus always did what pleased the Father, so the Father was always with Him.
q: If someone asked you, “Who is Jesus?” how would you answer?
Does your life now rely more on yourself, or, like Jesus, on the Father?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, open our eyes so that we truly know who Jesus is. Not staying only at knowledge, but truly knowing Him as the Christ, the Savior, the Lord of life. And let us learn Jesus' life: not living by ourselves but always seeking Your heart. May we also live in Your presence, because we long to do what pleases You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus therefore said to those Jews who had believed him, “If you remain in my word, then you are truly my disciples.
You will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.”
b: These two verses are among the most famous words in the whole Bible, and Jesus' most important definition of “true faith.” Many people love the sentence “the truth will make you free,” but overlook the most important condition before it:
Jesus did not say this to unbelievers but to “those Jews who had believed him.” This means:
Believing is not the finish line; the life of a true disciple is only beginning.
Many believe in Jesus but do not follow Him; accept the gospel but do not live in the truth.
“Remain” means to continue, to abide within, not to leave. Not an occasional inspiration; not zeal in meetings; not a brief pursuit; but living every day in His word.
And “keeping” is not only knowing but obeying, living out, and practicing.
True faith is not studying Jesus' words but letting Jesus' words become life.
Know the truth but do not practice it; like hearing sermons but do not change; know a great deal of spiritual knowledge but still live in the old self.
Only those who “remain in my word” are truly my disciples.
A true disciple is not one who calls Jesus Lord with the mouth but one whose life is changed by the truth.
It is not that we first know the truth and then obey; rather, we first become willing to obey, and then truly understand the truth.
Spiritual truth is not understood by the mind alone but opened up in obedience.
Many keep thinking, “I'll obey once I understand everything,” but in the kingdom of God it is often:
True truth does not stay in knowledge but enters life.
When a person begins to do the Lord's word, he truly realizes:
So forgiveness brings freedom; so humility brings grace; so self-denial brings life; so obeying the Holy Spirit gives more peace than relying on oneself.
Truth is not theory; it is a life truly lived out.
Then Jesus spoke the words that shook the world:
“And the truth will make you free.”
Doing whatever you want is freedom; having no restrictions is freedom; living by your feelings is freedom.
But the freedom Jesus speaks of is completely different.
Many people seem free but are actually bound by:
Sin; emotion; desire; pride; money; people's opinions; fear; wounds of the past.
True freedom is not doing whatever you want, but:
No longer being controlled by sin.
Truth is like light, shining on darkness; truth is like a blade, cutting bonds; truth is like a key, opening the prison.
And true freedom can be found only in Jesus.
He is the truth; His word is truth; His life is truth.
Apart from Jesus, people can never be truly free.
First, true faith is not brief belief but continual following. A true disciple is one who constantly abides in the Lord's word.
Second, knowing the truth is not the same as being free. Only those who practice the truth truly experience it.
Third, spiritual understanding often comes from obedience, not analysis. Only those willing to live it out will truly understand.
Fourth, the freedom the world gives is false freedom. True freedom is being released from sin and the old self.
Fifth, Jesus does not only tell us the truth; He Himself is the truth. Those who follow Him will truly be set free.
q: Is your present attitude toward the truth “knowing” or “practicing”?
Where in your life are you still bound, needing Jesus' truth to set you free?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, let us not only hear Your word but truly keep Your way. Let the truth not stay only in our minds but enter our lives. And set us free from every bond of sin and darkness, so that we may have true freedom in Jesus. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: They answered him, “We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone. How do you say, ‘You will be made free’?”
Jesus answered them, “Most certainly I tell you, everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin.
A bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever. A son remains forever.
If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.
b: This passage uncovers one of the deepest illusions of the human heart: people think they are free while they are actually living in bondage.
“We are Abraham’s offspring, and have never been in bondage to anyone.”
This statement is actually very ironic.
For in Israel's history they had been slaves in Egypt, slaves in Babylon, and were even then living under the Roman Empire. Yet they still said, “We have never been in bondage to anyone.”
The deepest bondage is not knowing that one is bound.
Many people today are the same:

Clearly living in sin, yet feeling very free; clearly controlled by emotion, yet feeling quite normal; clearly bound by people's opinions, yet thinking themselves independent; clearly living in pride, self, and selfish desire, yet believing they are in control of their lives.
The most terrible thing about sin is not only that it harms people but that it makes people lose their awareness.
So Jesus directly pointed out the real problem:
“Everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin.”
Jesus was not speaking of an occasional stumble but of a state of life controlled by sin.
When a person leaves God, life is naturally ruled by sin.
Sin is not only outward behavior but an inward power.
People think they are making choices, but often it is sin controlling them:

Wanting not to be angry, yet still exploding; wanting not to compare, yet still envying; wanting not to worry, yet unable to stop; wanting not to be proud, yet always wanting to prove oneself; wanting not to sin, yet repeating it again and again.
The greatest mark of a bondservant is:
Being unable to truly live the life he wants to live.
“For the desire to do what is good is present with me, but the doing of it is not.”
Because there is the power of sin within us.
“A bondservant doesn’t live in the house forever. A son remains forever.”
A bondservant has no inheritance, no identity, no security; he can only stay in the house for a time.
A son belongs to the house; a son has the Father's love; a son has an inheritance; a son has an identity; a son can remain in the house forever.
Sin makes people lose the identity of sons and live like bondservants; but the Father wants, through Him, to restore bondservants to sons.
“If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.”
What the world gives is false freedom:
Indulgence is called freedom; willfulness is called freedom; doing as you please is called freedom.
But in the end these become deeper bondage.
“I am finally no longer controlled by sin.”
And only Jesus can do this.
He has overcome sin; He has overcome death; He has broken the power of Satan; He gives us the life of a son.
So Jesus does not make us “feel free”; He truly releases us from within.
Sin; pride; fear; darkness; the world; the old self.
First, the greatest human problem is not knowing that we are bound. Pride makes people mistakenly think they are free.
Second, sin is not a single act but a power that rules people. Those who leave God naturally live in the slavery of sin.
Third, Jesus came not only to forgive sin but to set people free. He wants to restore our identity as sons.
Fourth, the world's freedom is false freedom. True freedom is no longer being controlled by sin and the old self.
Fifth, only Jesus can make people truly free. For only He is the Son, and only He can give us the life of a son.
q: Where in your life are you actually still bound, though you did not notice it before?
Today, are you willing to let Jesus truly set you free to live in the freedom of God's children?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, enlighten us to see the real bondage in our lives. Thank You for sending Jesus, not only to forgive us but to set us free. Let us no longer live in the slavery of sin but truly live out the identity and freedom of sons. May Your truth renew us every day, so that we receive true release in Christ. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: I know that you are Abraham’s offspring, yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.
I say the things which I have seen with my Father; and you also do the things which you have seen with your father.”
They answered him, “Our father is Abraham.” Jesus said to them, “If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.
But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do this.
You do the works of your father.” They said to him, “We were not born of sexual immorality. We have one Father, God.”
b: In this passage Jesus begins to bring the question to a deeper root. The Jews kept emphasizing:
What truly decides whom you belong to is not bloodline but life.
At the start of the passage Jesus said:
“I know that you are Abraham’s offspring.”
He acknowledged their physical descent. They were indeed Abraham's descendants. But then Jesus pointed out a more real problem:
“Yet you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place in you.”
The problem was not outside but inside.
It was not that they had not heard the truth, but that it “finds no place” in them.
The truth cannot get in; the life refuses to be changed; the old self resists God's light.
Truth is like a seed, but if the heart is too hard, too full, too proud, the word cannot enter.
Often people reject the truth not because they do not understand but because the truth will tear down their pride, ideas, and sovereignty.
The moment Jesus' light shone in, they did not repent but wanted to get rid of the light.
“I say the things which I have seen with my Father; and you also do the things which you have seen with your father.”
This sentence begins to enter the question of spiritual source.
Jesus' life came from the Father, so what He said was the Father's truth and what He lived out was the Father's life.
But the Jews' behavior showed another source.
Life reveals its source; whom a person belongs to inwardly is whom he lives out outwardly.
In their eyes, “Abraham's offspring” was the greatest spiritual security.
“If you were Abraham’s children, you would do the works of Abraham.”
A true son is not only of the same bloodline but of the same life.
Abraham's greatest mark was not national identity but:
Faith; obedience; receiving God's word; being willing to follow God.
Rejected the truth; opposed the Son of God; wanted to kill the one God sent.
Though they had Abraham's bloodline, they did not have Abraham's life.
A true Christian is not only:
Baptized; attending meetings; having a religious background; knowing a lot.

Those who truly belong to God love the truth, receive the light, and are willing to repent. If a person long refuses the truth and wants only to protect himself, it shows there is a problem with the source of life within.
Then Jesus pointed out once more:
“A man who has told you the truth which I heard from God.”
Jesus did not harm them; He only brought them the truth. But if people love darkness more than light, they will hate the truth.
Pride; falsehood; self-righteousness; the old self; darkness.
“You do the works of your father.”
This sentence foretells an even stronger exposure to come.
What truly decides whom a person belongs to is not religious identity but the nature of life.
First, what truly blocks the truth is not the mind but the heart. Many do not fail to understand; they are unwilling to let the truth in.
Second, the source of life within a person will show in outward behavior. Whatever life is like, behavior will be like.
Third, those who truly belong to God do not only have a religious background but have God's life. God values life, not only outward appearance.
Fourth, truth reveals what a person truly loves. Those who love the light draw near to Jesus; those who love darkness oppose Jesus.
Fifth, Abraham's true descendants are those who have Abraham's faith and a life of obedience.
q: Does your heart truly have room for God's truth?
Is the life you are living out now more like Abraham's faith or like the pattern of the world?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, make our hearts soft, not resisting Your truth. Remove from us the pride and self-righteousness within, so that we do not only have a spiritual appearance but truly live out a life that belongs to You. May Your word enter deeply into us, renewing and changing us, so that we become more and more like Jesus. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Therefore Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out and have come from God. For I haven’t come of myself, but he sent me.
Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.

You are of your father, the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks on his own; for he is a liar, and the father of lies.
But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.
Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?
He who is of God hears the words of God. For this cause you don’t hear, because you are not of God.”
b: This passage is one of Jesus' most severe and most truthful speeches. He directly uncovers the deepest root of a person's spiritual life:
Whom a person truly belongs to is seen not in religious appearance but in the source of life within.
“God is our Father.” But Jesus pointed out:
If God were truly your Father, you would surely love me.
Those who truly belong to the Father love the Son the Father sent.
“If God were your father, you would love me.”
Loving Jesus is not only religious feeling but proof of the source of life.
Those who truly know the Father will surely be drawn to Jesus; those who truly belong to God will surely love truth, love light, and love Christ.
If people reject Jesus, hate the truth, and oppose the light, however zealous their religion, it shows their life does not belong to God.
Then Jesus pointed out a deeper problem:
“Why don’t you understand my speech? Because you can’t hear my word.”
It was not that Jesus was unclear, but that the life within them refused to receive.
Here “can't hear” does not mean the ears could not hear but that the heart refused to submit.
Often when people cannot take in the truth, it is not an intelligence problem but a life problem.
The proud find it hard to take in the truth, because truth will tear down their throne.
Then Jesus spoke the most startling sentence of the whole passage:
“You are of your father, the devil.”
This is not an emotional insult but the revealing of a spiritual fact.
Because the qualities of life they lived out were the same as the devil's:
Rejecting the truth; hating the light; full of murderous intent; living in lies.
“He was a murderer from the beginning, and doesn’t stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him.”
He brings death through lies. The Garden of Eden was just so:
So every lie that draws people away from God finally leads them into death.
“You can be happy without God.” “Sin doesn't matter.” “People can be their own king.” “Just live for yourself.” “Pride is what gives you worth.”
All of these draw people away from the source of life.
“But because I tell the truth, you don’t believe me.”
Some people do not believe in Jesus not because they have not heard the truth but because the truth is too true.
Truth exposes human darkness, and darkness does not like to be lit up.
So sometimes people do not believe not because the evidence is insufficient but because the truth would require them to lay themselves down.
“Which of you convicts me of sin?”
Jesus could say this because He is completely holy.
He had many enemies, yet they could not find any real sin in Him.
His life itself was the most powerful testimony.
“He who is of God hears the words of God.”
Those who truly belong to God respond to God's word.
They may not fully understand at first, but within them there is longing, softness, and willingness.
And those who reject the truth to the end show that the root of their life is wrong.
First, those who truly belong to God will surely love Jesus, because Jesus is the one the Father sent.
Second, the greatest human problem is not failing to understand the truth but being unwilling to submit to it. If the heart is proud, the word cannot get in.
Third, Satan's main work is to use lies to draw people away from life.
Fourth, truth exposes darkness, so many resist truth. It is not that the light has a problem but that darkness is unwilling to be lit up.
Fifth, those who truly belong to God respond to God's word, because the source of their life is different.
q: When truth shines on you, is your first reaction surrender or resistance?
Are there lies of the world in your life that are still affecting you, drawing you away from God?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, make our hearts truly Yours. Remove from within us all the pride and darkness that resist the truth, so that we love Jesus, love the truth, and love the light. And keep us from being deceived by the world and its lies, but let us live every day in Your word. May we become people who truly hear Your voice and follow You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Then the Jews answered him, “Don’t we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon?”
Jesus answered, “I don’t have a demon, but I honor my Father and you dishonor me.
But I don’t seek my own glory. There is one who seeks and judges.
Most certainly, I tell you, if a person keeps my word, he will never see death.”
b: This passage shows us that when people cannot overcome the truth, they begin to attack the one who speaks it. And Jesus once again shows a completely different life: He does not argue for Himself or seek His own glory, but simply honors the Father and brings eternal life to people.
“Then the Jews answered him, ‘Don’t we say well that you are a Samaritan, and have a demon?’”
To the Jews, “Samaritan” was a term of contempt; “having a demon” directly denied the spiritual source of Jesus.
In other words, they not only rejected Jesus but treated the Son of God as a source of evil.
When the heart rejects the true light, it begins to call light darkness.
It was not that they had not heard the truth, but that the truth stung their pride. So they began to:
This is the very natural reaction of darkness toward light.
But Jesus' response was very calm:
“I don’t have a demon, but I honor my Father and you dishonor me.”
He was not carried away by emotion, did not fall into quarreling, and was not eager to prove Himself.
He simply pointed out one thing:
The core of Jesus' life was not “protecting Himself” but “glorifying the Father.”
For those who truly belong to God, the focus is not how much they have been wronged but:
Often people are easily hurt, angered, and drawn into arguments because the “self” is too big. The moment face is damaged, they want to strike back at once.
But Jesus was completely different. In Him there was no “self” to defend. So even when insulted, He remained at peace.
“But I don’t seek my own glory. There is one who seeks and judges.”
Jesus did not fight for His own glory. He entrusted everything to the Father.
True glory does not need to be grasped by oneself; true vindication does not need to be proved by oneself; true justice the Father will make clear.
This is a life of complete trust in the Father.
The pain of many people comes from:
Always wanting to prove themselves; always wanting to be seen; always wanting to be vindicated; always wanting to grasp glory.
The Father will judge. The Father will seek glory for Him.
Only such a life can truly rest.
Then Jesus suddenly declared a startling promise:
“If a person keeps my word, he will never see death.”
The “death” here is not only physical death.
For everyone's body will pass away. What Jesus spoke of is:
When people keep the Lord's word, abide in Him, and trust Him, they receive eternal life.
Though the body may die, the life lives forever.
So the true hope of a Christian is not:
Never departing this world; but rather:
Even in departing, entering eternal life.
Jesus did not let people escape death; He overcame death.
First, when truth exposes darkness, people often attack the one who speaks the truth, because darkness does not like to be lit up.
Second, Jesus did not seek glory for Himself but simply honored the Father. This is the most beautiful form of a life of self-denial.
Third, true rest comes from entrusting vindication and glory to the Father.
Fourth, worldly death is not the fearful thing; separation from God is. And Jesus can bring people into eternal life.
Fifth, keeping the Lord's word is not only a religious act but abiding in life. Such a person has already passed from death into life.
q: Do you still often want to stand up for yourself and prove yourself?
Do you truly believe that those who keep Jesus' word have already passed from death into life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, let us learn Jesus' life: not seeking glory for ourselves but simply honoring You. When we are misunderstood or wronged, help us entrust everything to You, believing that You will surely judge rightly. And thank You for giving eternal life through Jesus, so that we no longer live in death and fear but in eternal hope. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Then the Jews said to him, “Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham died, as did the prophets; and you say, ‘If a man keeps my word, he will never taste of death.’
Are you greater than our father, Abraham, who died? The prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?”
Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our God.
You have not known him, but I know him. If I said, ‘I don’t know him,’ I would be like you, a liar. But I know him and keep his word.
b: This passage is a deep spiritual conflict. Jesus spoke of eternal life, but the Jews stayed with physical death. Jesus spoke of heavenly life, but they thought only by earthly logic.
So without the Holy Spirit's enlightenment, even standing before the truth, a person cannot truly understand.
“Now we know that you have a demon.”
They were not merely doubting Jesus but condemning Him more and more fiercely.
When truth keeps shining on people, if they are unwilling to repent, the heart grows harder and harder.
“Even the greatest spiritual figures died; how dare you say that those who keep your word will never die?”
Eternal life; life joined to God; life that overcomes the power of death.
This is the limit of the earthly view. If people look only at this life, they can never understand eternal life.
“Are you greater than our father, Abraham, who died?”
This sentence actually touched on the truth.
Jesus is not only greater than Abraham; He is even the source of Abraham's life.
But they could not see it.
They honored Abraham yet rejected the Christ to whom Abraham looked forward.
This is also a common contradiction in religion:
Honoring what God did in the past while rejecting what God is doing now.
“Who do you make yourself out to be?”
This is in fact the core question of the whole chapter.
A teacher? A prophet? A heretic? Or the Son of God?
What a person understands of Jesus decides his eternal direction.
“If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing.”
Once again He showed His self-denial.
He never exalted Himself; never grasped for glory; never relied on people's praise to prove Himself.
He gave all glory entirely to the Father.
Those who truly come from God do not keep exalting themselves; they let people see the Father.
Many people's service becomes weary, wounded, and full of comparison, because they are still pursuing their own glory.
But Jesus was completely free, because He cared only for the Father's glory.
“It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say that he is our God.”
With their mouths they said they knew God, but when the Son who truly came from God stood before them, they rejected Him.
This is a theme repeated throughout the chapter.
Religious knowledge is not knowing God; religious zeal is not knowing God; outward piety is not knowing God.
Those who truly know God will surely know Jesus.
His relationship with the Father was not theoretical but a oneness of life.
He did not only know things about the Father; He truly lived in the Father.
Then He added a very heavy sentence:
“If I said, ‘I don’t know him,’ I would be like you, a liar.”
Saying with the mouth they knew God, while their lives rejected God.
“But I know him and keep his word.”
Those who truly know God will surely obey God.
To know is not only knowledge but a connection of life and living it out.
First, if people use only an earthly view, they cannot understand heavenly life. Eternal life is not only that the body does not die but being joined to God forever.
Second, what a person understands of Jesus decides his eternal direction. He is not only a prophet but the Lord of life.
Third, those who truly come from God do not seek their own glory. Jesus lived completely in the Father's glory.
Fourth, a religious appearance is not truly knowing God. Those who truly know God will surely receive Jesus.
Fifth, those who truly know God will also surely keep God's word. Obedience is the proof of true knowing.
q: Does your knowledge of God now stay at the level of knowledge, or do you truly live in a relationship?
When you do things, do you care more about your own glory or God's glory?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, let us not stay only in religious knowledge but truly know You. Help us, like Jesus, not to pursue our own glory but to seek Your glory alone. And let us not only say with our mouths that we know You, but truly keep Your word in daily life and live out a life that belongs to You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day. He saw it, and was glad.”
The Jews therefore said to him, “You are not yet fifty years old! Have you seen Abraham?”
Jesus said to them, “Most certainly, I tell you, before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”
Therefore they took up stones to throw at him, but Jesus was hidden, and went out of the temple, having gone through the middle of them, and so passed by.
b: This passage is one of the most startling revelations in the Gospel of John. Jesus does not only declare that He is greater than Abraham; He declares directly:
This is also why in the end the Jews wanted to pick up stones to throw at Him. For they knew very well that Jesus was using for Himself a title that only God can use.
At the start of the passage Jesus said:
“Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day.”
Abraham lived about two thousand years before Jesus' birth, yet Jesus said:
Abraham had looked forward to Him.
The true focus of the whole Old Testament is Christ.
The promise Abraham waited for; the story of offering Isaac; God providing the lamb; the hope of the Messiah; the promise of the kingdom of God:
Though Abraham did not see with his own eyes Jesus the Word made flesh, by faith he saw in advance God's plan of salvation.
True faith rejoices at seeing Christ.
Then the Jews immediately objected with the eyes of the flesh:
“You are not yet fifty years old! Have you seen Abraham?”
Once again they pulled heavenly truth back down to earthly logic.
Not knowing that the one standing before them was not only the Son of Man but the eternal Son of God.
So Jesus spoke a sentence that shook the whole place:
“Before Abraham came into existence, I AM.”
This is exactly the name God used when He appeared to Moses in Exodus 3:
Here Jesus directly applied God's name to Himself.
He is not created; He is not an ordinary prophet; He is not a great teacher; He is the eternally existing God.
Abraham had a beginning; Jesus has no beginning.
Abraham was created; Jesus is the Creator.
Time cannot limit Him; death cannot overcome Him; history is not His starting point.
He transcends history, yet entered history to save people.
“Therefore they took up stones to throw at him.”
Because in the eyes of the Jews this was “blasphemy.” They knew Jesus was declaring Himself equal to God.
But the problem was not that Jesus was wrong; it was that they refused to accept it.
The true light came into the world, yet darkness did not receive the light.
“But Jesus was hidden, and went out of the temple.”
Not because He was afraid but because His hour had not yet come.
The whole Gospel of John repeatedly reminds us:
Jesus' life was entirely in the Father's timing. No one could take His life ahead of time.
He would go to the cross, but not because people overcame Him; it was because He willingly gave Himself.
First, the true center of the whole Bible is Jesus Christ. The promises of the Old Testament and the fulfillment of the New all point to Him.
Second, if people use only the eyes of the flesh, they cannot know Jesus. Heavenly truth must be received by faith.
Third, Jesus is not only a historical figure; He is the eternal God. He is the “I AM,” the One who is who He is.
Fourth, the greatest problem people have with Jesus is not insufficient evidence but unwillingness to accept that He is God. For if He is truly God, people must surrender.
Fifth, Jesus' life was completely under the Father's governance. He was not driven by circumstances but lived in the Father's timing.
q: Has your understanding of Jesus truly grown to “He is Lord, He is God”?
Is your life pushed along by circumstances, or do you live in the Heavenly Father's timing and leading?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for giving Jesus to us, so that we can truly know You. Open our spiritual eyes, so that we do not treat Jesus merely as a teacher or religious figure but truly know Him as the eternal God, the Lord of life. And help us learn from Jesus to live in Your timing and will, not driven by the world but simply obeying You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”
Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents; but, that the works of God might be revealed in him.
b: This passage opens a very important theme: God's way of looking at a problem is completely different from man's.
When people see suffering, their first reaction is often:
“Who is at fault?” “Who caused this?” “Did someone do something wrong?”
But when Jesus saw suffering, what He cared about more was:
“How God will reveal His glory and His works in it.”
“As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.”
Many people passed that blind man every day without truly “seeing” him. Some saw a problem, some saw trouble, some saw pity, but Jesus saw a life.
Jesus' vision was never only on the surface. He did not only look at a person's defects; He saw what God could do in that person.
This was a very common idea among the Jews then:
Suffering must be the result of sin. So if someone is born disabled, sick, or suffering, someone must have sinned.
The disciples' question actually represents the natural way people think:
When meeting a problem, first look for the sinner; first look for who is responsible; first look for the cause.
But often the greatest human problem is not not knowing the answer but:
Who has the problem; who should take responsibility; who did wrong.
God's glory; God's work; God's salvation.
“This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents.”
Jesus was not denying that sin brings pain but pointing out:
Not all suffering can be reduced to “who sinned.”
People live in a fallen world, where sickness, death, and brokenness are the result of sin entering the world. But we cannot define every pain as “God is punishing.”
Often what hurts people most in suffering is not the pain itself but being condemned.
From birth this blind man may have lived under the gaze of:
“There must be something wrong with you.” “You must be cursed.” “You are not normal.”
But Jesus broke this culture of condemnation.
Then He spoke a very important sentence:
“But, that the works of God might be revealed in him.”
Jesus did not keep the focus on the past but turned to what God would do in the future.
This does not mean God deliberately lets people suffer in order to perform miracles, but:
Even when people are broken, God can still bring in grace, healing, and glory.
The world sees suffering as an ending; Jesus sees suffering as the starting point of God's work.
What people see is blindness; what Jesus sees is the glory God is about to show.
Often we too are like the disciples:
“Why?” “Who is to blame?” “Where is the problem?”
“Are you willing to let me work here?”
First, Jesus truly sees people. He does not look only at problems but sees lives.
Second, people naturally like to condemn and look for causes. But what Jesus brings is grace and hope.
Third, not all suffering can be simply explained as “the result of sin.” Do not be quick to judge another's pain.
Fourth, God can show His glory in people's brokenness. Difficulty is not an obstacle to God's work; it may be the starting point.
Fifth, the key to a spiritual life is not to keep asking “why,” but to be willing to let God work in our lives.
q: When you meet a problem, is your first reaction condemnation and complaint, or seeking God's work?
Are you willing to believe that even in your brokenness, God can still show His glory?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, change the way we look at things. Let us no longer be quick to condemn, judge, or look for someone to blame, but learn like Jesus to see Your heart and Your works. When we face our own weakness and suffering, let us believe that You can still show glory in our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
b: This passage records the words Jesus spoke before healing the blind man. He did not only want to heal a person's eyes; He wanted people to see:
The true focus of life is not to stay in the problem but to seize the time God gives and live out God's will.
“That the works of God might be revealed in him.”
“I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day.”
This sentence is full of mission and urgency.
Jesus knew that His coming into the world was no accident; He had a charge from the Father. His life was not lived for Himself but to complete the Father's work.
Not “when I have time,” not “depending on the situation,” not “when it is convenient.”
Those who truly live in God's will know:
Life is not to be lived carelessly; life is not only for comfort; time is not only for satisfying ourselves.
God gave us life with a mission.
Still having opportunity; still having time; still having grace; still having life; still having light.
Jesus knew His time on earth was limited. Night was coming: the hour of the cross, persecution, and judgment was near.
So He treasured every moment to fulfill the Father's will.
Later; I'll love God when I have time; I'll serve after retirement; I'll obey once things are better; I'll follow the Lord when I'm ready.
Life does not always offer opportunity. One day “night is coming,” and no one can work.
This does not only refer to death but to the closing of opportunity.
Today; now; the opportunity God is giving.
Because what truly matters is not how long we live but whether we have fulfilled God's will.
“While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
Once again He declared that He is the light.
The world's greatest problem is not lack of knowledge but lack of light.
Without light, people cannot see direction; without light, people take darkness as normal; without light, people get lost, stumble, and hurt one another.
And Jesus came to bring light into the world.
Reveals truth; reveals sin; reveals God's love; reveals the direction of life; reveals true hope.
And what is special about this passage is that:
Jesus had just seen a blind man, and now He declared:
“I am the light of the world.”
True blindness is not only that the physical eyes cannot see; true darkness is being without Jesus.
Some people can see with their eyes yet are completely dark in spirit; some are physically normal yet their lives are lost.
Only Jesus can truly make people see.
First, the true value of life is in completing God's work. Not living only for ourselves but living out God's will.
Second, the time God gives is limited. Treasure the opportunity we still have today to love God, serve God, and follow God.
Third, spiritual people have a sense of mission. They know life is not wasted but sent.
Fourth, Jesus is the true light of the world. Without Him, however clever people are, they still live in darkness.
Fifth, true darkness is not the night outside but a life without Jesus. True light is not knowledge but Christ Himself.
q: Is your life now more about completing your own plans or completing God's work?
Have you truly let Jesus' light shine into every corner of your life?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, let us treasure every day You give, not wasting time but living in Your will. Help us, like Jesus, to have a sense of mission from You, knowing that what truly matters in life is to complete Your work. And let Jesus' light shine on us every day, so that we no longer live in darkness and lostness. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,
and said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.
b: This passage paints a wonderful picture. The way Jesus healed the blind man seems very unreasonable, even strange. But much of the time, God’s work simply does not follow human reason or human methods.
And the heart of this passage is this:
True seeing is not only a miracle; it is obedience.
“He spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud.”
If we were that blind man, we might be very confused:
“Lord, aren’t You going to heal me? Why are You putting mud on my eyes?”
By human logic, what a blind person needs most is clarity; yet Jesus first made his sight even more clouded.
This is exactly how God’s ways so often go beyond our understanding.
God does not first explain; He first asks us to trust. He does not first make us understand; He first asks us to obey.
Miracles are not produced by human methods but by the power of God.
Jesus could easily have healed him with a single word, yet He chose a process.
Because God did not only want to heal his eyes; He wanted to build his faith.
“Go, wash in the pool of Siloam.”
Jesus did not make him see right away; He gave him a command.
And for a blind man, this was not easy.
go with mud all over his eyes; feel his way forward; walk through the crowds; endure other people’s stares; and make his way step by step to the pool.
On the road to a miracle, faith needs obedience.
Many people want a miracle right away, but are not willing to walk the road of obedience.
But this blind man is precious.
The Scripture does not record him complaining, questioning, or analyzing. He did not say:
“Why do I have to go?” “Will this even work?” “Is this reasonable?” “What if I’m not healed?”
True faith does not wait until it fully understands before acting; it is willing to obey even before it sees.
“So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.”
Not by standing still and analyzing; not by standing there doubting; not by rational calculation.
being willing to do what the Lord said.
This is also a key difference in many people’s spiritual lives.
Some keep waiting to understand everything before they obey; but God often lets people see only as they obey.
Then the Scripture adds a special note:
John records this name on purpose, because there is spiritual meaning in it.
Jesus was sent by the Father; and the blind man also had to go to the pool called “Sent.”
True seeing comes from obeying God’s sending.
Today many people cannot see in their spirit, not because God has no light, but because they are unwilling to obey.
Obedience opens the eyes; obedience brings light; obedience brings a changed life.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, God’s ways often go beyond human reason. Do not limit God with human logic.
Second, God often asks people to obey first, and then lets them see. Faith does not wait to understand everything before taking a step.
Third, the road of a true miracle requires action. The blind man did not sit and wait; he got up and went to wash.
Fourth, obedience is the key to having our spiritual eyes opened. Those who do not obey will find it hard to truly see God.
Fifth, Jesus did not only heal a man’s eyes; He was building his faith and his life.
q: Is there something God has already told you to do, yet you are still stuck in analyzing and watching from the sidelines?
Are you willing, like the blind man, to obey and move forward even before you can see?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, give us a simple, obedient heart. When You lead us on roads we do not understand, help us not to stay stuck in doubt and analysis, but to be willing to believe Your word. Open our spiritual eyes, so that through obedience we may see Your work and experience Your real power and grace. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: The neighbors therefore, and those who saw that he was blind before, said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”
Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.” He said, “I am he.”
They therefore were asking him, “How were your eyes opened?”
He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”
Then they asked him, “Where is he?” He said, “I don’t know.”
b: This passage shows us something very real: when a person is truly changed by Jesus, people are amazed.
Because the change Jesus brings is not a little touch-up on the outside; it is a life turned upside down.
“The neighbors, and those who saw that he was blind before, said…”
This blind man’s past life was fixed:
sitting; blind; begging; ignored; labeled by others.
Everyone was used to seeing him this way. In people’s eyes, his life would probably always be like this.
But when Jesus stepped in, everything changed.
“Isn’t this the one who used to sit and beg?”
Some said he was; some said he wasn’t; some said he only looked like him.
True change makes a person unrecognizable.
When Jesus shines His light on someone, the look in his eyes, his life, his spirit, and his direction all change.
Those who were in darkness begin to have light; those who were in despair begin to have hope; those who were bound begin to have freedom.
This kind of life change cannot be faked.
And the blind man did something very important:
He did not hide his past. He did not deny that he had been blind. He openly admitted:
“Yes, I am the blind beggar you used to know.”
Those who have truly experienced grace do not need to pretend to be perfect. Because what is truly glorious is not “how great I am,” but:
Many people are afraid to give their testimony because they fear others will find out about their past.
But in fact, the darkness of our past is exactly what shows how real the light of Jesus is.
People are curious about real life change. Because the world seldom sees someone who has truly been renewed.
This is a very precious sentence.
His theology was not yet complete; his knowledge of Jesus was still limited; he did not even know where Jesus was.
A true testimony does not necessarily need a lot of knowledge; a true testimony is:
“This is what I was, and now, because of Jesus, I am different.”
This is the most powerful gospel.
Then he described it very simply:
“He made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”
No complicated theory; no religious jargon; no debate.
a change that came after obedience.
Often the thing people find hardest to argue against is not a theory but a real life.
Although he did not yet fully know Jesus, he had truly experienced Jesus.
Often a person’s spiritual life begins in just this way:
first experiencing grace, then gradually knowing the Lord more deeply.
God often does not first make people understand everything, but first lets them meet Him.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, those who truly meet Jesus have their lives changed. And this change is real and visible.
Second, the world is used to people staying as they are. But Jesus can turn a life around.
Third, a true testimony is not about being perfect but about being real. Those who dare to admit they once were blind bring the most glory to God.
Fourth, the greatest power of the gospel is a changed life. Not empty theory, but real experience.
Fifth, many people first experience Jesus and then slowly come to know Him. God leads people step by step to know Him more deeply.
q: In what areas has your life already been changed by Jesus?
Are you willing to boldly share who you used to be, and who you have become because of Jesus?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for changing our lives through Jesus. Help us not to hide our past, but to be willing to openly testify to Your grace. And let our lives be truly renewed by You, so that people who see our change may see Your glory. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: They brought him who had been blind to the Pharisees.
It was a Sabbath when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
Again therefore the Pharisees also asked him how he received his sight. He said to them, “He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see.”
Some therefore of the Pharisees said, “This man is not from God, because he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How can a man who is a sinner do such signs?” There was division among them.
b: This passage shows us something very deep: when God truly works, people’s hearts are revealed.
Some see a miracle and draw closer to God; some see a miracle and resist Him all the more.
The problem is not the miracle but the human heart.
“They brought him who had been blind to the Pharisees.”
This should have been a cause for joy:
A man born blind could now see.
But no one rejoiced for him first; instead they immediately took him to the religious leaders to be “examined.”
the religious system was beginning to feel uneasy.
Because Jesus’ work went beyond what they could control.
Often, when people see God’s real work, their first response is not joy but a question:
“Does it fit our rules?” “Is it done our way?” “Does it match tradition?”
Then the Scripture makes a special point:
“Now it was the Sabbath on the day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.”
John does not record this sentence casually.
Because this is the very heart of the conflict.
The Pharisees always put Sabbath regulations above human need. To them:
keeping the rules mattered more than a person being healed; religious form mattered more than life.
But Jesus came not to abolish the Sabbath but to restore its true meaning.
The true Sabbath is not religious pressure; it is:
life restored; entering God’s grace; receiving true rest.
Then the Pharisees asked the man again:
The man again answered very simply:
“He put mud on my eyes, I washed, and I see.”
Jesus did it; I obeyed; and the result is that I see.
A true testimony does not need to be complicated. Because the real power belongs to God Himself.
Yet verse 16 immediately reveals two different reactions.
“This man is not from God, because he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.”
The biggest problem with these people was this:
they placed their own religious framework above God.
“God can only work in the way we understand.”
So even when they saw a miracle, they still refused to believe.
Often the greatest blindness is not failing to see a miracle, but this:
God has acted, and yet people refuse to accept it.
Because God’s way goes beyond their own ideas.
“How can a man who is a sinner do such signs?”
These people were beginning to be shaken by the truth.
They did not yet fully believe in Jesus, but at least they were willing to face the facts honestly:
If Jesus were not from God, how could He do such a thing?
When the true light comes, the crowd divides.
Because Jesus does not only bring comfort; He also exposes the human heart.
Some are willing to surrender; some hold on to their own opinions.
They saw the same work of God, yet reacted in completely different ways.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, when religion loses life, it easily puts rules above people. God values life more than form.
Second, if people have fixed ideas, they may reject God’s true work. Do not limit God with human frameworks.
Third, a true miracle makes honest people begin to think about the truth. God’s work stirs people’s hearts.
Fourth, Jesus came not only to heal eyes but to reveal hearts. Those who are truly blind are not necessarily those who cannot see with their eyes.
Fifth, a true testimony is simple: Jesus did it, I obeyed, and I was changed.
q: Have you ever rejected something God was doing because of your own ideas?
When God’s work goes beyond your understanding, are you still willing to believe and obey?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, guard our hearts so that we do not limit You with our own ideas as the Pharisees did. Help us love life more than form, and love truth more than tradition. And give us honest, tender hearts, so that when You work, we are willing to surrender and believe. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Therefore they asked the blind man again, “What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?” He said, “He is a prophet.”
The Jews therefore didn’t believe concerning him, that he had been blind, and had received his sight, until they called the parents of him who had received his sight,
and asked them, “Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?”
His parents answered them, “We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;
but how he now sees, we don’t know; or who opened his eyes, we don’t know. He is of age. Ask him. He will speak for himself.”
His parents said these things because they feared the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if any man would confess him as Christ, he would be put out of the synagogue.
Therefore his parents said, “He is of age. Ask him.”
b: This passage shows us that when people face Jesus, what is exposed is not only their faith, but also their fear.
Some grow bolder and bolder as they experience God; others, even after seeing God at work, shrink back for fear of what people think.
The Scripture begins with the Pharisees asking the blind man again:
“What do you say about him, because he opened your eyes?”
They were not simply wanting an answer; they were looking for grounds to condemn Jesus.
But the blind man’s answer was growing:
Now he was beginning to know Jesus more deeply.
Those who truly meet Jesus come to know Him more and more deeply.
Faith is not completed all at once, but is illuminated step by step.
“The Jews therefore did not believe concerning him that he had been blind.”
When the facts clashed with their ideas, they chose to deny the facts.
Because if they admitted this miracle was real, it meant they would have to face Jesus all over again.
Often people have not failed to see God at work, but rather:
they are unwilling to accept the truth behind God’s work.
The miracle was real. No one could deny it.
“But how he now sees, we don’t know.”
In fact they very likely knew something, at least that it had to do with Jesus.
But they chose to protect themselves.
Because anyone who publicly confessed Jesus as the Christ would be put out of the synagogue.
This was a very serious matter at that time.
Being put out of the synagogue meant not only being unable to attend gatherings; it could also mean:
losing social ties; losing religious standing; losing work and community; being shut out by the whole society.
So for these parents, the pressure was enormous.
say little; protect themselves; avoid taking a stand.
This is also the spiritual condition of many people.
They do not entirely disbelieve in Jesus, but rather:
they do not dare to stand openly on Jesus’ side.
people’s opinions; group pressure; loss of benefits; being misunderstood; being rejected.
But this passage also forms a sharp contrast:
The blind man, though he had only just begun to know Jesus, grew bolder and bolder; his parents, though they knew more, shrank back in fear.
Often what truly keeps people from following the Lord is not lack of evidence, but:
Yet the road of truth has always required a choice.
“For they loved the glory that comes from men more than the glory that comes from God.”
This becomes the reason people cannot truly follow the Lord.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, truly knowing Jesus is gradual. Those who follow the Lord will know Him more and more.
Second, if people already have their position fixed, they may reject the truth even after seeing a miracle. Pride makes people deny the facts.
Third, many people do not lack belief; they simply do not dare to admit it, because they fear what people think and the cost.
Fourth, fear of man keeps people from standing openly on the side of truth. But only those who fear God can be truly free.
Fifth, true faith grows bolder and bolder. Even as the pressure increases, it is willing to stand on Jesus’ side.
q: Are there areas where you actually know the truth but, out of fear of people, do not dare to admit it?
If today it cost you something to stand with Jesus, would you still stand on His side?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, remove from us the fear of man. When the world, our circumstances, and people’s opinions press upon us, give us strength to stand boldly on the side of truth. And let our knowledge of Jesus grow deeper and deeper, not staying only at knowing about Him, but truly being willing to follow Him to the end. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
They said to him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
He answered them, “I told you already, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”
b: This passage is wonderful. Because we see a man who was born blind and had no standing now beginning to see the truth more clearly than the religious leaders.
And all this is not because he knew a great deal, but because:
“So they called a second time the man who was blind.”
Why did they still need to ask again?
Because they could not let it go.
What truly troubled them was not that the miracle was unclear, but:
this man had truly been blind, and now truly saw.
So they were left with only one way—to force him to deny Jesus.
“Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”
On the surface it sounded devout:
But in fact they were pressing the man to go along with their own conclusion.
“A truly devout person would admit that Jesus is wrong.”
Often people say “for God” with their mouths, when in fact they are protecting their own system.
But the blind man’s answer was very powerful:
“Whether he is a sinner, I don’t know. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”
This sentence is one of the most striking testimonies in the whole chapter.
He had no profound theology; no complicated debate; there was even much he did not understand.
The greatest power of a true testimony is not theory but reality.
The world can argue theology with you; but it is hard to deny someone who has truly been changed.
“You can discuss many things, but I was blind and now I see. That is a fact.”
This is also the truest power of the gospel.
A person who has truly met Jesus:
has a changed life; a changed way of seeing; a changed direction; and light begins to shine inside.
“What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
They did not want to understand; they wanted to find a loophole.
Some people are not seeking truth but seeking to refute truth.
So the blind man’s boldness began to grow.
“I told you already, and you didn’t listen.”
the problem was not the evidence but the human heart.
Often people do not lack answers; they are unwilling to accept the answer.
Then he said something with both humor and courage:
“Why do you want to hear it again? You don’t also want to become his disciples, do you?”
This sentence is almost like a challenge in the form of a question.
that a man who had only just received his sight would dare to speak to the Pharisees this way.
those who truly experience Jesus begin to have courage inside.
Before, he could only sit and beg; now he dared to speak up for the truth.
This is the change that comes when light enters a life.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, what truly keeps people from believing is often not a lack of evidence but a heart unwilling to change. The Pharisees had seen the miracle, yet still refused the truth.
Second, the testimony with real power is a changed life. “Though I was blind, now I see.”
Third, we do not need to wait until we fully understand theology to testify to Jesus. Those who have truly experienced the Lord can bear witness to Him.
Fourth, when religion loses the truth, it begins to control and manipulate people. A faith that truly belongs to God leads people into the light.
Fifth, those who truly meet Jesus begin to have courage inside. Because light drives away darkness and fear.
q: Have you truly experienced Jesus changing your life?
If someone asked you today, “What has Jesus done for you?” how would you answer?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You for bringing us out of darkness into light. Let us not only know about Jesus, but truly experience the power of His life-changing work. And give us courage, not to hide Your light in this world, but to boldly bear witness to You. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: They insulted him and said, “You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
We know that God has spoken to Moses. But as for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”
The man answered them, “How amazing! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshiper of God, and does his will, he listens to him.
Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
They answered him, “You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?” Then they threw him out.
b: This passage is a very sharp contrast. On one side are the religious leaders, who think they can see and understand the truth; on the other is the man who has just received his sight and understands the truth more and more.
And the greatest irony is this:
The ones who are truly blind are not the man who once could not see, but those who refuse the true light.
The Scripture begins with the Pharisees, furious, saying:
“You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.”
“We are the truly orthodox, the ones who truly belong to God.”
One of the chief marks of religious pride is:
constantly stressing one’s identity, background, and tradition.
those who truly belong to God are not defined by outward religious identity but are willing to receive God’s light.
“As for this man, we don’t know where he comes from.”
In fact it was not that they truly did not know, but:
they were unwilling to admit it.
Often people’s greatest problem is not that they have no light, but that they refuse to accept it.
Yet the blind man’s answer grew more and more powerful:
“A man who opened my eyes, and you religious experts cannot even tell where he comes from?”
The one who was thought to “not understand” now saw more clearly than the religious leaders.
true spiritual sight is not an accumulation of knowledge, but whether one is willing to receive the true light.
“We know that God doesn’t listen to sinners, but if anyone is a worshipper of God, and does his will, he listens to him.”
This is not a complete theological formula, but he was already beginning to know God through experience.
If Jesus were not from God, He could not do such a miracle.
“Since the world began it has never been heard of that anyone opened the eyes of someone born blind.”
What Jesus did was not ordinary healing; He did something never done before.
He did not merely repair a problem; it was creative restoration.
Only the God who creates people can open the eyes of one born blind.
“If this man were not from God, he could do nothing.”
A man once looked down on as lowly, blind, and a beggar was now closer to the truth than the Pharisees.
Because he was willing to face God’s work honestly.
The Pharisees’ reaction completely exposed their darkness.
“You were altogether born in sins, and do you teach us?”
When people have no truth left to stand on, they begin to:
They did not want to be reminded; did not want to admit they might be wrong; did not want to humble themselves.
rejected by the religious system; shut out by the community; regarded as unqualified.
when the world throws a person out, Jesus draws even closer to him.
Sometimes people lose their standing on earth, yet enter more deeply into the presence of God.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, true blindness is not the inability to see with the eyes but the refusal of the true light. Pride makes people deny even what they clearly see.
Second, true spiritual sight does not depend on how much knowledge we have but on whether we are willing to receive God. The humble find it easier to understand the truth.
Third, what Jesus did is work that only God can do. He does not merely heal; He brings new creation.
Fourth, religious pride makes people unable to accept correction. Because the old self fears being torn down more than anything.
Fifth, sometimes being rejected by people for the truth actually brings us closer to Jesus. The world’s rejection does not mean God’s rejection.
q: Have you ever rejected God’s correction because of your pride?
If you were rejected by people today for the truth’s sake, would you still be willing to stand on Jesus’ side?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, remove from us all pride and spiritual blindness. Let us not only have religious knowledge, but be truly willing to receive Your light. And make us like the blind man, answering Your work simply and honestly, so that even if we are misunderstood for it, we are still willing to stand on the side of truth. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”
Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”
He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.
b: This passage is very gentle, and very moving. The blind man had just been thrown out by the religious leaders for testifying to Jesus. In people’s eyes, he had lost:
his community; his religious standing; his security; people’s acceptance.
But right after he was thrown out, Jesus came to find him Himself.
This is the most beautiful part of the gospel:
When the world rejects you, Jesus does not leave you.
“Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him…”
Jesus knew his situation; knew his loneliness; knew he had paid a price for the truth.
So Jesus came looking for him on His own initiative.
Often people think they have been cast away by the world, when in fact it is the beginning of a deeper experience of the Lord.
when people lose the world’s support, they often hold on to Jesus more truly.
“Do you believe in the Son of God?”
Notice that Jesus did not first comfort him:
“You’ve had a hard time.” “You were wronged.”
Jesus brought him straight to the heart of deeper faith:
not merely experiencing a miracle, but knowing who Jesus is.
the miracle is not the destination; truly knowing Christ is the goal.
“Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”
Inside him there was already a heart willing to believe.
He was not arguing proudly; not refusing; not doubting.
“I am willing to believe; please tell me who He is.”
Those who have truly received grace have softened hearts. Because they know:
“You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”
Before, his physical eyes could not see; now not only were his eyes opened, but his spiritual eyes also began to truly see.
This is not only seeing Jesus’ outward appearance, but:
Many people can see Jesus with their physical eyes but not in their spirit; many Pharisees faced Jesus every day yet did not know Him.
But this man who had been blind now truly saw.
Then verse 38 is the most beautiful response in the whole passage:
No complicated theology; no lengthy theory; only a heart willing to surrender.
This is an extremely important verse.
Because worship belongs to God alone.
Jesus is not merely a prophet, a teacher, or a healer; He is the Son of God, He is Lord.
And this man’s journey of life is also wonderful:
At first, all he knew was:
True faith is knowing Jesus more and more.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, when people are rejected for the truth, Jesus draws closer to them. The Lord does not abandon those who stand for Him.
Second, the miracle is not the destination; truly knowing Jesus is the goal. Having our eyes healed is only the beginning.
Third, God reveals Himself to those who are truly willing to believe. A tender heart can truly see the Lord.
Fourth, true spiritual sight is recognizing that Jesus is the Son of God. This matters more than physical sight.
Fifth, true faith finally leads to worship. When people truly know Jesus, they bow down before Him.
q: At what stage is your knowledge of Jesus right now?
Do you truly worship Him from the heart and surrender to Him?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, thank You that when we are rejected by the world, You still come looking for us Yourself. Do not only heal our outward problems, but open our spiritual eyes, so that we may truly know that Jesus is the Son of God and the Lord of life. May we not only experience grace, but be willing to believe in You and worship You with all our heart. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment, that those who don’t see may see; and that those who see may become blind.”
Those of the Pharisees who were with him heard these things, and said to him, “Are we also blind?”
Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would have no sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.
b: This passage is the conclusion of John chapter 9. The whole chapter speaks of “blindness” and “seeing,” but in the end Jesus points out:
What is truly terrible is not physical blindness, but being spiritually blind without knowing you are blind.
The Scripture begins with Jesus saying:
“For judgment I came into this world.”
Jesus’ first coming was not to finally condemn the world, but to bring light.
But when light enters the world, people’s hearts are naturally exposed.
those who receive the light begin to see; those who reject the light find their darkness growing deeper.
“that those who don’t see may see.”
This does not refer only to the man born blind. It refers even more to:
those who know they need God.
Those who can truly be enlightened by God are often not those who think they are great, but those who admit:
“I cannot see; I need the Lord; I need the light.”
Such people are the ones who truly see.
The blind man was just like this.
He could not see with his eyes, yet he was willing to obey Jesus; willing to admit his need; willing to receive the light.
So in the end, not only were his eyes opened, but in his spirit he truly saw Christ.
“and that those who see may become blind.”
to understand the law; to understand Scripture; to understand truth; to be the most spiritual; to be nearest to God.
But precisely because they “thought they saw,” they rejected the true light.
Pride is the deepest spiritual blindness.
Because a proud person does not seek light; he thinks he already has it.
They had actually understood that Jesus was pointing at them.
But they still refused to admit it.
True blindness is often not ignorance but unwillingness to admit.
Finally Jesus said something very profound:
“If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, ‘We see.’ Therefore your sin remains.”
that those who are truly blind have no sin.
if people admit they cannot see and are willing to humbly seek God, there is still the possibility of being healed.
But the most terrible thing is:
being blind and yet insisting that you can see.
Such people do not repent; do not seek the light; do not receive Jesus.
Often people’s greatest problem is not weakness but:
not admitting that they need God.
sinners find it easier to believe; the self-righteous find it hardest to accept the gospel.
those who know they are blind will look for light; those who think they have light will reject it.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, Jesus came to bring light into people’s lives. And light reveals a person’s true spiritual condition.
Second, those who can truly see are those who admit they need God. Humility is the beginning of receiving light.
Third, the greatest spiritual blindness is thinking you can see. Pride keeps people from receiving the truth.
Fourth, the people God finds hardest to heal are not the weak but the self-righteous. Because the self-righteous do not feel they need grace.
Fifth, true wisdom is to admit every day that we need the light of Jesus. Apart from the Lord, we will all fall into darkness again.
q: Is there some spiritual pride in you that makes you think you already “see very clearly”?
Today, are you willing to humbly come to Jesus once again and ask Him to enlighten you?
pr: Dear Heavenly Father, guard our hearts so that we do not fall into the pride of the Pharisees. Let us always stay humble and admit that we need Your light. Open our spiritual eyes every day, so that we do not merely know a lot on the outside, but truly know You and follow You. May the light of Jesus always shine on our lives. We pray in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, amen.

v: “Most certainly, I tell you, one who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheep fold, but climbs up some other way, is a thief and a robber.
But one who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens the gate for him, and the sheep listen to his voice. He calls his own sheep by name, and leads them out.
Whenever he brings out his own sheep, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, for they know his voice.
They will by no means follow a stranger, but will flee from him; for they don’t know the voice of strangers.”
Jesus spoke this parable to them, but they didn’t understand what he was telling them.
b: This passage is the beginning of Jesus’ famous teaching on the “Good Shepherd.” And the background is very important—
Chapter 9 had just ended, with the Pharisees throwing the man who had been blind and now saw out of the synagogue.
Those who should have shepherded the people had no love, no truth, and no compassion.
who the true shepherd is, and who the false ones are.
“He who doesn’t enter by the door into the sheepfold, but climbs up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber.”
In those days a sheepfold usually had one proper entrance. The true shepherd goes in by the door; only a thief sneaks over the wall.
True leadership from God is open, above-board, and in line with God’s heart; false spiritual leaders are actually stealing sheep.
On the outside they look like shepherds, but in fact they are for themselves.
The marks of a thief are:
using the sheep; controlling the sheep; harming the sheep; taking the sheep; not loving the sheep.
But the true shepherd is different.
“But he who enters in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.”
Jesus is the true shepherd who comes from the Father. He does not steal people; He was sent to save them.
True shepherding that belongs to God is not control, but leading lives into God.
Those who truly belong to the Lord recognize the Lord’s voice.
Not by outward control; not by religious pressure; not by intimidation.
a real knowledge of the Lord in their lives.
The sheep may not know much, but they recognize the shepherd’s voice.
In the same way, those who truly belong to God are stirred inside by the truth, and respond to the voice of Jesus.
“He calls his own sheep by name.”
In Jesus’ eyes, we are not a faceless sheep in the flock.
He knows us; knows our names; knows our weakness; knows our tears; knows our life story.
This world often treats people as numbers, tools, and functions, but Jesus knows His sheep by name.
True shepherding is not just managing a group; it is a relationship of life.
“he goes before them, and the sheep follow him.”
Jesus does not stand behind with a whip to drive the sheep; He goes ahead and leads the way.
True leadership from God is not domination but example.
Jesus Himself first walked the road of the cross; first denied Himself; first obeyed; first loved.
So the sheep are willing to follow Him.
Because a true shepherd does not just give orders; he lives out the way.
“They will by no means follow a stranger.”
Those who truly belong to the Lord begin to have discernment inside.
the voice of fear; the voice of accusation; the voice of pride; the voice of selfish desire; the voice of men; the voice of religious control.
But the Lord’s sheep slowly learn to discern:
which voice sounds like Jesus, and which does not.
Because the voice of Jesus carries:
truth; peace; life; love; holiness; light.
Without a humble heart, even if Jesus Himself speaks, people may not understand.
Spiritual truth is understood not through cleverness but through willingness to follow.
This passage reminds us of five things:
First, a true shepherd who belongs to God leads people closer to God, not controls them. The thief is for himself; the shepherd is for the sheep.
Second, Jesus is the true Good Shepherd. He came from the Father and lays down His life for the sheep.
Third, those who truly belong to the Lord recognize the Lord’s voice. In their lives they respond to the truth.
Fourth, Jesus knows each sheep by name. You are not someone overlooked.
Fifth, true leadership is not domination but example. Jesus Himself walks in front.
q: Whose voice do you listen to most each day right now? The world’s? Your emotions’? Or the Lord’s?
Do you truly believe that Jesus knows you and is leading your life?
